info.title: Survey web/SSR path for HTMX gaps (@explore subagent)

parts.text:
Survey the Pathland repo's web/SSR path in depth (be very thorough) and produce a precise inventory plus a gap list. This is READ-ONLY research; do not modify anything.

Repo root: /Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland

Context: Pathland is a binary opcode UI protocol (16-byte opcodes) with an SSR HTML renderer + a vanilla-JS hydration client (app.js) used by Spring Boot and Quarkus demos. The user wants to turn it into a credible replacement for HTMX for enterprise SRE teams (server-driven UI, minimal client JS, WebSocket deltas). I need to know exactly what exists today to build a gap list.

Please inventory and report:

1. **The web client (app.js)**: Find every copy of app.js under lib/java/*/src/main/resources/**. For the main/reference copy, report: what it does (hydration by data-pathland-id, PLPL batch decode, delta application), how it sends raw-input events over the WebSocket, whether it has any reconnection logic / heartbeat / backoff / session-resync, how it handles server disconnect, error handling, and whether it is a self-contained versioned artifact or a demo helper. Quote key function names.

2. **SSR HTML renderers**: 
   - Java: lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/com/pathland/render/html/... — list EVERY view component that has an HTML element mapping and the exact element/tag + attributes it emits (e.g. Text->span, Button->button, TextField->input[type=text]?, Toggle->checkbox?, Slider->input[type=range]?, Picker->select?, Spacer->div). Note which components from spec/PRIMITIVES.md have NO mapping yet. Report whether it emits: form semantics (input name=, label for=, form=), ARIA attributes, role attributes.
   - Rust: lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs — same question, which components map to what HTML elements, and whether the Rust one is used by any runnable demo today.

3. **Demos (transport + sessions)**: In lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo and pathland-quarkus-demo: how the WebSocket is set up (path, session handling), how per-session State/PersistentState works, how frames/events are batched (transport batching policy), and whether there is ANY observability/metrics/logging beyond plain logging. Any CSRF / origin / auth checks on the WS? Any heartbeat or reconnect support?

4. **Existing tests**: What test coverage exists for the HTML renderers (golden/round-trip), the app.js client (is there ANY JS test?), and the transport.

5. **Repo conventions**: Where would a reusable JS client and docs naturally live (is there a docs/ dir, a lib/js or similar, a top-level README structure)? List existing docs/*.md files.

Return a structured report with file paths + line numbers for the key items, a component-by-HTML-element mapping table, and a clear "gaps" list organized by: transport resilience, accessibility, form semantics, observability, security, and client artifact/versioning. Do not propose fixes — just inventory what exists and what does not.

Let me start by exploring the repo structure to understand the layout, then dig into each area.

Let me start with broad exploration in parallel.
I'll survey the repo thoroughly. Let me start with broad structural exploration.

197:     /// Border CSS, decoded from `BORDER_WIDTH`/`BORDER_COLOR`/`BORDER_RADIUS`/
198:     /// `BORDER_EDGES` (empty when the node has no border).
199:     fn border_style(&self) -> String {
200:         let Some(width_bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::BORDER_WIDTH) else {
201:             return String::new();
202:         };
203:         let width = f32::from_bits(*width_bits);
204:         let color = self
205:             .properties
206:             .get(&property_id::BORDER_COLOR)
207:             .copied()
208:             .unwrap_or(0xFF00_0000);
209:         let edges = self
210:             .properties
211:             .get(&property_id::BORDER_EDGES)
212:             .copied()
213:             .unwrap_or(border_edges::ALL);
214: 
215:         let (r, g, b, a) = unpack_color(color);
216:         let mut css = String::new();
217:         for (flag, side) in [
218:             (border_edges::TOP, "top"),
219:             (border_edges::LEADING, "left"),
220:             (border_edges::BOTTOM, "bottom"),
221:             (border_edges::TRAILING, "right"),
222:         ] {
223:             if edges & flag != 0 {
224:                 css.push_str(&format!("border-{side}:{width}px solid rgba({r},{g},{b},{a});"));
225:             }
226:         }
227:         if let Some(radius) = self.properties.get(&property_id::BORDER_RADIUS) {
228:             let radius = f32::from_bits(*radius);
229:             if radius != 0.0 {
230:                 css.push_str(&format!("border-radius:{radius}px;"));
231:             }
232:         }
233:         css
234:     }
235: }

237: /// Unpack a `0xAARRGGBB` color into `(r, g, b, alpha)` where `alpha` is `0..1`.
238: fn unpack_color(argb: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32, f32) {
239:     let r = (argb >> 16) & 0xFF;
240:     let g = (argb >> 8) & 0xFF;
241:     let b = argb & 0xFF;
242:     let a = ((argb >> 24) & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0;
243:     (r, g, b, a)
244: }
245: 
246: /// A `0xAARRGGBB` color as a CSS `rgba(r,g,b,a)` string.
247: fn rgba(argb: u32) -> String {
248:     let (r, g, b, a) = unpack_color(argb);
249:     format!("rgba({r},{g},{b},{a})")
250: }
251: 
252: /// A `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` hint as CSS: `FILL` (-1) → `100%`, `HUG_CONTENT` (-2) →
253: /// `max-content`, otherwise pixels.
254: fn size_css(v: f32) -> String {
255:     if v == pathland_core::size::FILL {
256:         "100%".to_string()
257:     } else if v == pathland_core::size::HUG_CONTENT {
258:         "max-content".to_string()
259:     } else {
260:         format!("{v}px")
261:     }
262: }
263: 
264: /// The column count of a `GRID` from its `WIDTH` property (cell-axis count);
265: /// `FILL`/absent → auto-fit.
266: fn grid_columns(node: &Node) -> Option<u32> {
267:     let w = node.f32_property(property_id::WIDTH, -1.0);
268:     if w <= 0.0 {
269:         None
270:     } else {
271:         Some(w.round() as u32)
272:     }
273: }

275: /// Convert days since the Unix epoch (negative = before 1970) to a Gregorian
276: /// `(year, month, day)` using the civil-from-days algorithm.
277: fn days_to_date(days: i32) -> (i32, u32, u32) {
278:     let z = i64::from(days) + 719_468;
279:     let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;
280:     let doe = z - era * 146_097;
281:     let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
282:     let y = yoe + era * 400;
283:     let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
284:     let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
285:     let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
286:     let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
287:     let y = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
288:     (y as i32, m as u32, d as u32)
289: }
290: 
291: /// Millis of day → `(hours, minutes, seconds)`.
292: fn millis_to_hms(millis: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32) {
293:     let total = millis / 1000;
294:     (total / 3600, (total % 3600) / 60, total % 60)
295: }

297: /// Event-surfacing `data-*` attributes for a hydration client, from
298: /// `EVENT_LISTENERS` / `ACTION_ID` / `BINDING_ID`.
299: fn event_attrs(node: &Node) -> String {
300:     let mut attrs = String::new();
301:     if let Some(m) = node.properties.get(&property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS) {
302:         if *m != 0 {
303:             attrs.push_str(&format!(" data-event-listeners=\"{m}\""));
304:         }
305:     }
306:     if let Some(a) = node.properties.get(&property_id::ACTION_ID) {
307:         attrs.push_str(&format!(" data-action-id=\"{a}\""));
308:     }
309:     if let Some(b) = node.properties.get(&property_id::BINDING_ID) {
310:         attrs.push_str(&format!(" data-binding-id=\"{b}\""));
311:     }
312:     attrs
313: }
314: 
315: /// ARIA attributes from `ROLE` / `STATE` / `ENABLED`.
316: fn aria_attrs(node: &Node) -> String {
317:     let mut attrs = String::new();
318:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::ROLE) {
319:         let role = match f32::from_bits(*bits) as u8 {
320:             1 => "button",
321:             2 => "link",
322:             3 => "heading",
323:             6 => "textbox",
324:             7 => "slider",
325:             8 => "switch",
326:             9 => "checkbox",
327:             12 => "tab",
328:             16 => "scrollbar",
329:             19 => "menuitem",
330:             _ => "",
331:         };
332:         if !role.is_empty() {
333:             attrs.push_str(&format!(" role=\"{role}\""));
334:         }
335:     }
336:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::STATE) {
337:         match f32::from_bits(*bits) as u8 {
338:             1 => attrs.push_str(" aria-disabled=\"true\""),
339:             2 => attrs.push_str(" aria-current=\"true\""),
340:             3 => attrs.push_str(" aria-pressed=\"true\""),
341:             4 => attrs.push_str(" aria-selected=\"true\""),
342:             _ => {}
343:         }
344:     }
345:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::ENABLED) {
346:         if *bits == 0 {
347:             attrs.push_str(" disabled");
348:         }
349:     }
350:     attrs
351: }

353: /// Applies opcode frames to a retained node map and renders it as HTML.
354: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
355: pub struct HtmlRenderer {
356:     nodes: BTreeMap<u32, Node>,
357: }
358: 
359: impl HtmlRenderer {
360:     /// Create an empty renderer.
361:     #[must_use]
362:     pub fn new() -> Self {
363:         Self::default()
364:     }
365: 
366:     /// Apply a transport `Frame` (a self-contained opcode frame + string
367:     /// section), mutating the retained description. The frame may come from
368:     /// [`frame_from_slices`] (in-process), a network decoder, or a ring.
369:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame) {
370:         for op in frame.opcodes() {
371:             match op.category() {
372:                 category::TREE => self.apply_tree(op.command(), op),
373:                 category::STYLE => self.apply_style(op.command(), op, frame),
374:                 _ => {}
375:             }
376:         }
377:     }
378: 
379:     /// Apply a frame from raw opcodes + a string section, building an in-memory
380:     /// [`Frame`] (via the in-process transport seam) and delegating to
381:     /// [`Self::apply_frame`].
382:     pub fn apply(&mut self, opcodes: &[Opcode], strings: &[u8]) {
383:         let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE);
384:         let frame = frame_from_slices(&mut slots, strings, opcodes);
385:         self.apply_frame(&frame);
386:     }
387: 
388:     fn apply_tree(&mut self, command: u8, op: Opcode) {
389:         match command {
390:             tree::CREATE_NODE => {
391:                 let id = op.a();
392:                 let component = op.b() as u16;
393:                 self.nodes.insert(id, Node::new(component));
394:             }
395:             tree::DELETE_NODE => {
396:                 self.nodes.remove(&op.a());
397:             }
398:             tree::INSERT_CHILD => {
399:                 let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
400:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
401:                     node.children.push(child);
402:                 }
403:             }
404:             tree::REMOVE_CHILD => {
405:                 let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
406:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
407:                     node.children.retain(|&c| c != child);
408:                 }
409:             }
410:             tree::MOVE_CHILD => {
411:                 let (parent, child, index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c());
412:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
413:                     node.children.retain(|&c| c != child);
414:                     let index = (index as usize).min(node.children.len());
415:                     node.children.insert(index, child);
416:                 }
417:             }
418:             _ => {}
419:         }
420:     }
421: 
422:     fn apply_style(&mut self, command: u8, op: Opcode, frame: &Frame) {
423:         match command {
424:             style::SET_TEXT => {
425:                 if let Some(text) = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok() {
426:                     if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
427:                         node.text = Some(text.to_string());
428:                     }
429:                 }
430:             }
431:             style::SET_PROPERTY => {
432:                 let property = (op.b() & 0xFFFF) as u16;
433:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
434:                     let vt = (op.b() >> 16) as u8;
435:                     if vt == value_type::STRING {
436:                         if let Some(text) = frame.arena_str(op.c()).ok() {
437:                             node.strings.insert(property, text.to_string());
438:                         }
439:                     } else {
440:                         node.properties.insert(property, op.c());
441:                     }
442:                 }
443:             }
444:             style::SET_DATE => {
445:                 if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
446:                     // B = days since epoch (I32), C = millis of day (U32).
447:                     node.date = Some((op.b() as i32, op.c()));
448:                 }
449:             }
450:             _ => {}
451:         }
452:     }
453: 
454:     /// Render the subtree rooted at `root` as a full HTML document.
455:     #[must_use]
456:     pub fn render(&self, root: u32) -> String {
457:         let body = self.render_node(root);
458:         format!(
459:             "<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n<head>\n<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n\
460:              <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n\
461:              <title>Pathland</title>\n\
462:              <style>\n\
463:              body {{ font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 16px; }}\n\

467:              .pathland-toggle input[role=\"switch\"] {{ appearance: none; width: 44px; height: 24px; border-radius: 12px; background: #bbb; cursor: pointer; position: relative; transition: background 0.15s; }}\n\

484:     /// Render the subtree rooted at `root` as an HTML fragment (no `<html>`).
485:     #[must_use]
486:     pub fn render_fragment(&self, root: u32) -> String {
487:         self.render_node(root)
488:     }

490:     fn render_node(&self, id: u32) -> String {
491:         let Some(node) = self.nodes.get(&id) else {
492:             return String::new();
493:         };
494:         let children: String = node
495:             .children
496:             .iter()
497:             .map(|&child| self.render_node(child))
498:             .collect();
499:         let data_id = format!(" data-pathland-id=\"{id}\"");
500:         let css = format!("{}{}", node.style_css(), node.border_style());
501:         let style = style_attr(&css);
502:         let event = event_attrs(node);
503:         let aria = aria_attrs(node);
504: 
505:         match node.component {
506:             component_type::VSTACK => self.wrap_stack(id, "column", node, &children, &css, &event, &aria),
507:             component_type::HSTACK => self.wrap_stack(id, "row", node, &children, &css, &event, &aria),
508:             component_type::LAZY_VSTACK => {
509:                 self.wrap_stack(id, "column", node, &children, &css, &event, &aria)
510:             }
511:             component_type::LAZY_HSTACK => {
512:                 self.wrap_stack(id, "row", node, &children, &css, &event, &aria)
513:             }
514:             component_type::TEXT => {
515:                 let text = escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default());
516:                 format!("<span{data_id}{event}{aria}{style}>{text}</span>")
517:             }
518:             component_type::BUTTON => {
519:                 // Composite Override Mode: children present → custom body.
520:                 let body = if node.children.is_empty() {
521:                     escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default())
522:                 } else {
523:                     children
524:                 };
525:                 format!("<button{data_id}{event}{aria}{style}>{body}</button>")
526:             }
527:             component_type::TOGGLE => {
528:                 let toggle_style = node.f32_property(property_id::TOGGLE_STYLE, 0.0).round() as u8;
529:                 let checked = if node.checked() { " checked" } else { "" };
530:                 let body = if node.children.is_empty() {
531:                     format!(
532:                         "<span class=\"pathland-text\">{}</span>",
533:                         escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default())
534:                     )
535:                 } else {
536:                     format!("<div class=\"pathland-custom-body\">{children}</div>")
537:                 };
538:                 match toggle_style {
539:                     1 => format!(
540:                         "<label{data_id}{event}{aria} class=\"pathland-toggle\"{style}><input type=\"checkbox\"{checked}>{body}</label>"
541:                     ),
542:                     2 => {
543:                         let pressed = if node.checked() { "true" } else { "false" };
544:                         format!(
545:                             "<button{data_id}{event}{aria} type=\"button\" aria-pressed=\"{pressed}\"{style}>{body}</button>"
546:                         )
547:                     }
548:                     _ => format!(
549:                         "<label{data_id}{event}{aria} class=\"pathland-toggle\"{style}><input type=\"checkbox\" role=\"switch\"{checked}>{body}</label>"
550:                     ),
551:                 }
552:             }
553:             component_type::SPACER => {
554:                 let css = format!("flex:1;{css}");
555:                 format!("<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"{css}\"></div>")
556:             }
557:             component_type::SLIDER => {
558:                 let min = node.f32_property(property_id::MIN_VALUE, 0.0);
559:                 let max = node.f32_property(property_id::MAX_VALUE, 1.0);
560:                 let value = node.f32_property(property_id::VALUE, min);
561:                 let body = if node.children.is_empty() {
562:                     format!(
563:                         "<span class=\"pathland-text\">{}</span>",
564:                         escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default())
565:                     )
566:                 } else {
567:                     format!("<div class=\"pathland-custom-body\">{children}</div>")
568:                 };
569:                 format!(
570:                     "<label{data_id}{event}{aria} class=\"pathland-slider\"{style}><input type=\"range\" min=\"{min}\" max=\"{max}\" step=\"any\" value=\"{value}\">{body}</label>"
571:                 )
572:             }
573:             component_type::TEXT_FIELD => {
574:                 let value = escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default());
575:                 let label = escape(
576:                     node.strings
577:                         .get(&property_id::LABEL)
578:                         .map(String::as_str)
579:                         .unwrap_or_default(),
580:                 );
581:                 let prompt = escape(
582:                     node.strings
583:                         .get(&property_id::PROMPT)
584:                         .map(String::as_str)
585:                         .unwrap_or_default(),
586:                 );
587:                 let input_type = if node.f32_property(property_id::IS_SECURE, 0.0) != 0.0 {
588:                     "password"
589:                 } else {
590:                     "text"
591:                 };
592:                 format!(
593:                     "<label{data_id}{event}{aria} class=\"pathland-textfield\"{style}><span class=\"pathland-label\">{label}</span><input type=\"{input_type}\" value=\"{value}\" placeholder=\"{prompt}\"></label>"
594:                 )
595:             }
596:             component_type::TEXT_EDITOR => {
597:                 let value = escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default());
598:                 format!("<textarea{data_id}{event}{aria} rows=\"4\"{style}>{value}</textarea>")
599:             }
600:             component_type::IMAGE => {
601:                 let src = escape(
602:                     node.strings
603:                         .get(&property_id::IMAGE_SOURCE)
604:                         .map(String::as_str)
605:                         .unwrap_or_default(),
606:                 );
607:                 format!("<img{data_id}{event}{aria} src=\"{src}\"{style}>")
608:             }
609:             component_type::COLOR => {
610:                 let color = node.u32_property(property_id::COLOR, 0xFF00_0000);
611:                 // Layout-greedy (SwiftUI Color): expands to the available space
612:                 // unless a size modifier constrains it.
613:                 format!(
614:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch;background-color:{};{css}\">{children}</div>",
615:                     rgba(color)
616:                 )
617:             }
618:             component_type::SHAPE => {
619:                 let kind = node.f32_property(property_id::SHAPE_KIND, 0.0).round() as u8;
620:                 let fill = node.u32_property(property_id::COLOR, 0xFF00_0000);
621:                 let w = node.f32_property(property_id::WIDTH, 100.0);
622:                 let h = node.f32_property(property_id::HEIGHT, 100.0);
623:                 let base = format!(
624:                     "width:{};height:{};background-color:{};{css}",
625:                     size_css(w),
626:                     size_css(h),
627:                     rgba(fill)
628:                 );
629:                 let shape_css = match kind {
630:                     0 | 4 => "border-radius:50%;",
631:                     2 => {
632:                         let r = node.f32_property(property_id::BORDER_RADIUS, 8.0);
633:                         return format!("<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"{base}border-radius:{r}px;\"></div>");
634:                     }
635:                     3 => "border-radius:9999px;",
636:                     5 => {
637:                         return format!(
638:                             "<svg{data_id}{event}{aria} width=\"100\" height=\"100\" viewBox=\"0 0 100 100\"><rect width=\"100\" height=\"100\" fill=\"{}\"/></svg>",
639:                             rgba(fill)
640:                         );
641:                     }
642:                     _ => "",
643:                 };
644:                 format!("<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"{base}{shape_css}\"></div>")
645:             }
646:             component_type::DIVIDER => {
647:                 let width = node.f32_property(property_id::BORDER_WIDTH, 1.0);
648:                 let color = node
649:                     .properties
650:                     .get(&property_id::COLOR)
651:                     .copied()
652:                     .map(rgba)
653:                     .unwrap_or_else(|| "rgba(0,0,0,0.2)".to_string());
654:                 format!(
655:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"height:0;border-top:{width}px solid {color};\"></div>"
656:                 )
657:             }
658:             component_type::PROGRESS_VIEW => {
659:                 let indeterminate = node.f32_property(property_id::IS_INDETERMINATE, 0.0) != 0.0
660:                     || node.f32_property(property_id::PROGRESS, -1.0) < 0.0;
661:                 if indeterminate {
662:                     format!("<div{data_id} class=\"pathland-spinner\"{style}></div>")
663:                 } else {
664:                     let value = node.f32_property(property_id::PROGRESS, 0.0);
665:                     let max = node.f32_property(property_id::MAX_VALUE, 1.0);
666:                     format!(
667:                         "<progress{data_id}{event}{aria} value=\"{value}\" max=\"{max}\"{style}></progress>"
668:                     )
669:                 }
670:             }
671:             component_type::GAUGE => {
672:                 let min = node.f32_property(property_id::MIN_VALUE, 0.0);
673:                 let max = node.f32_property(property_id::MAX_VALUE, 1.0);
674:                 let value = node.f32_property(property_id::VALUE, min);
675:                 let pct = if max > min {
676:                     ((value - min) / (max - min)).clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 100.0
677:                 } else {
678:                     0.0
679:                 };
680:                 format!(
681:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} class=\"pathland-gauge\"{style}><div style=\"width:{pct}%\"></div></div>"
682:                 )
683:             }
684:             component_type::GRID | component_type::LAZY_VGRID | component_type::LAZY_HGRID => {
685:                 let cols = grid_columns(node);
686:                 let gap = node
687:                     .spacing()
688:                     .map(|s| format!("gap:{s}px;"))
689:                     .unwrap_or_default();
690:                 let template = cols
691:                     .map(|n| format!("grid-template-columns:repeat({n},1fr);"))
692:                     .unwrap_or_default();
693:                 let flow = if node.component == component_type::LAZY_HGRID {
694:                     "grid-auto-flow:column;grid-auto-columns:1fr;"
695:                 } else {
696:                     ""
697:                 };
698:                 format!(
699:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"display:grid;{template}{flow}{gap}{css}\">{children}</div>"
700:                 )
701:             }
702:             component_type::SCROLLVIEW => {
703:                 format!("<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"overflow:auto;{css}\">{children}</div>")
704:             }
705:             component_type::ZSTACK => {
706:                 let inner: String = node
707:                     .children
708:                     .iter()
709:                     .map(|&child| {
710:                         let child_html = self.render_node(child);
711:                         if child_html.is_empty() {
712:                             String::new()
713:                         } else {
714:                             format!("<div style=\"position:absolute;inset:0\">{child_html}</div>")
715:                         }
716:                     })
717:                     .collect();
718:                 format!(
719:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} style=\"position:relative;width:100%;height:100%;{css}\">{inner}</div>"
720:                 )
721:             }
722:             component_type::STEPPER => {
723:                 let min = node.f32_property(property_id::MIN_VALUE, 0.0);
724:                 let max = node.f32_property(property_id::MAX_VALUE, 100.0);
725:                 let value = node.f32_property(property_id::VALUE, min);
726:                 let step = node.f32_property(property_id::STEP_VALUE, 1.0);
727:                 format!(
728:                     "<input{data_id}{event}{aria} type=\"number\" min=\"{min}\" max=\"{max}\" step=\"{step}\" value=\"{value}\"{style}>"
729:                 )
730:             }
731:             component_type::DATE_PICKER => {
732:                 let mode = node.f32_property(property_id::DATE_PICKER_MODE, 0.0).round() as u8;
733:                 let (t, value) = match node.date {
734:                     Some((days, millis)) => match mode {
735:                         1 => {
736:                             let (hh, mm, _) = millis_to_hms(millis);
737:                             ("time", format!("{hh:02}:{mm:02}"))
738:                         }
739:                         2 => {
740:                             let (y, m, d) = days_to_date(days);
741:                             let (hh, mm, _) = millis_to_hms(millis);
742:                             (
743:                                 "datetime-local",
744:                                 format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}T{hh:02}:{mm:02}"),
745:                             )
746:                         }
747:                         _ => {
748:                             let (y, m, d) = days_to_date(days);
749:                             ("date", format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}"))
750:                         }
751:                     },
752:                     None => ("date", String::new()),
753:                 };
754:                 format!("<input{data_id}{event}{aria} type=\"{t}\" value=\"{value}\"{style}>")
755:             }
756:             component_type::PICKER => {
757:                 let selected = node.u32_property(property_id::SELECTION, 0);
758:                 let options: String = node
759:                     .children
760:                     .iter()
761:                     .enumerate()
762:                     .map(|(i, &child)| {
763:                         let label = self
764:                             .nodes
765:                             .get(&child)
766:                             .and_then(|n| n.text.clone())
767:                             .unwrap_or_default();
768:                         let sel = if i as u32 == selected { " selected" } else { "" };
769:                         format!("<option value=\"{i}\"{sel}>{}</option>", escape(&label))
770:                     })
771:                     .collect();
772:                 format!("<select{data_id}{event}{aria}{style}>{options}</select>")
773:             }
774:             component_type::MENU => {
775:                 let label = escape(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or_default());
776:                 format!(
777:                     "<div{data_id}{event}{aria} role=\"menu\"{style}><button type=\"button\">{label}</button>{children}</div>"
778:                 )
779:             }
780:             component_type::COLOR_PICKER => {
781:                 let color = node.u32_property(property_id::COLOR_VALUE, 0xFF00_0000);
782:                 let hex = format!(
783:                     "#{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}",
784:                     (color >> 16) & 0xFF,
785:                     (color >> 8) & 0xFF,
786:                     color & 0xFF
787:                 );
788:                 format!("<input{data_id}{event}{aria} type=\"color\" value=\"{hex}\"{style}>")
789:             }
790:             component_type::COMMENT => String::new(),
791:             _ => String::new(),
792:         }
793:     }

795:     fn wrap_stack(
796:         &self,
797:         id: u32,
798:         direction: &str,
799:         node: &Node,
800:         children: &str,
801:         css: &str,
802:         event: &str,
803:         aria: &str,
804:     ) -> String {
805:         let gap = node
806:             .spacing()
807:             .map(|s| format!("gap:{s}px;"))
808:             .unwrap_or_default();
809:         let margins = node
810:             .content_margins()
811:             .map(|m| format!("padding:{m}px;"))
812:             .unwrap_or_default();
813:         format!(
814:             "<div data-pathland-id=\"{id}\"{event}{aria} style=\"display:flex;flex-direction:{direction};{gap}{}{}{css}\">{children}</div>",
815:             node.alignment_css(),
816:             margins,
817:         )
818:     }
819: }

821: /// A `style="…"` attribute for a non-empty CSS fragment.
822: fn style_attr(css: &str) -> String {
823:     if css.is_empty() {
824:         String::new()
825:     } else {
826:         format!(" style=\"{css}\"")
827:     }
828: }

830: /// Escape text for inclusion in an HTML body.
831: fn escape(input: &str) -> String {
832:     input
833:         .replace('&', "&")
834:         .replace('<', "<")
835:         .replace('>', ">")
836:         .replace('"', """)
837:         .replace('\'', "'")
838: }

1: //! Batching policy and buffering for network transport.
2: //!
3: //! `Batcher` accumulates frames against a [`BatchPolicy`] and flushes a single
4: //! serialized batch when either the time interval since the first buffered
5: //! opcode elapses **or** the accumulated byte size reaches the threshold —
6: //! first trigger wins.
7: 
8: use alloc::vec::Vec;
9: use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
10: 
11: use pathland_core::Opcode;
12: 
13: use crate::batch::encode_batch;
14: use crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST;
15: 
16: /// Default time interval before a batch is flushed (4 ms).
17: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(4);
18: /// Default max batch byte size (conservative network frame / MTU).
19: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_BYTES: usize = 1400;
20: 
21: /// Flush thresholds for network batching.
22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
23: pub struct BatchPolicy {
24:     /// Flush when this much time has elapsed since the first buffered opcode.
25:     pub max_interval: Duration,
26:     /// Flush when the accumulated batch reaches this many bytes.
27:     pub max_batch_bytes: usize,
28: }
29: 
30: impl BatchPolicy {
31:     /// Create a policy from a time interval and a max batch size.
32:     pub const fn new(max_interval: Duration, max_batch_bytes: usize) -> Self {
33:         Self {
34:             max_interval,
35:             max_batch_bytes,
36:         }
37:     }
38: 
39:     /// The default policy: 4 ms interval, 1400-byte batches.
40:     pub const fn default_policy() -> Self {
41:         Self::new(DEFAULT_MAX_INTERVAL, DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_BYTES)
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: impl Default for BatchPolicy {
46:     fn default() -> Self {
47:         Self::default_policy()
48:     }
49: }
50: 
51: /// Accumulates frames into a batch and flushes per [`BatchPolicy`].
52: ///
53: /// The arena is append-only; the batcher ships the bytes appended since the
54: /// last flush (tracked by arena length). If the arena shrank (a `META::RESET`),
55: /// the pending arena is reset so the next flush starts fresh.
56: #[derive(Debug)]
57: pub struct Batcher {
58:     policy: BatchPolicy,
59:     /// Frame count of the first buffered frame.
60:     frame_count: u32,
61:     /// Opcodes buffered since the last flush.
62:     opcodes: Vec<Opcode>,
63:     /// Arena bytes appended since the last flush.
64:     pending_arena: Vec<u8>,
65:     /// Arena length at the last flush.
66:     last_arena_len: usize,
67:     /// When the first opcode of the current batch was buffered.
68:     started: Option<Instant>,
69:     /// Size trigger latched on push.
70:     size_triggered: bool,
71: }
72: 
73: impl Batcher {
74:     /// Create a batcher with the given policy.
75:     pub fn new(policy: BatchPolicy) -> Self {
76:         Self {
77:             policy,
78:             frame_count: 0,
79:             opcodes: Vec::new(),
80:             pending_arena: Vec::new(),
81:             last_arena_len: 0,
82:             started: None,
83:             size_triggered: false,
84:         }
85:     }
86: 
87:     /// Create a batcher with the default policy (4 ms / 1400 B).
88:     pub fn default_policy() -> Self {
89:         Self::new(BatchPolicy::default())
90:     }
91: 
92:     /// Whether no opcodes are currently buffered.
93:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
94:         self.opcodes.is_empty()
95:     }
96: 
97:     /// Number of opcodes buffered since the last flush (diagnostics).
98:     pub fn pending_opcodes(&self) -> usize {
99:         self.opcodes.len()
100:     }
101: 
102:     /// Approximate bytes that would be shipped on flush (diagnostics).
103:     pub fn pending_bytes(&self) -> usize {
104:         self.opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE + self.pending_arena.len() + crate::batch::BATCH_HEADER + 4
105:     }
106: 
107:     /// Record a frame (opcodes + the arena's used portion `[0..cursor)`),
108:     /// accumulating the arena delta. Returns `true` if the size trigger fired.
109:     pub fn push_frame(&mut self, frame_count: u32, opcodes: &[Opcode], arena_used: &[u8]) -> bool {
110:         if self.started.is_none() {
111:             self.started = Some(Instant::now());
112:             self.frame_count = frame_count;
113:         }
114:         if arena_used.len() < self.last_arena_len {
115:             // Arena was reset; restart the pending buffer.
116:             self.pending_arena.clear();
117:             self.last_arena_len = 0;
118:         }
119:         self.pending_arena.extend_from_slice(&arena_used[self.last_arena_len..]);
120:         self.last_arena_len = arena_used.len();
121:         self.opcodes.extend_from_slice(opcodes);
122: 
123:         self.size_triggered |= self.pending_bytes() >= self.policy.max_batch_bytes;
124:         self.size_triggered
125:     }
126: 
127:     /// Whether the time interval has elapsed since the first buffered opcode.
128:     pub fn interval_elapsed(&self) -> bool {
129:         match self.started {
130:             Some(t) => t.elapsed() >= self.policy.max_interval,
131:             None => false,
132:         }
133:     }
134: 
135:     /// Serialize and reset the current buffer, returning the batch bytes.
136:     ///
137:     /// Flushes when `force` is true or either policy trigger fired. Returns
138:     /// `None` when nothing is buffered.
139:     pub fn flush(&mut self, force: bool) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
140:         if self.opcodes.is_empty() {
141:             return None;
142:         }
143:         let should_flush = force || self.size_triggered || self.interval_elapsed();
144:         if !should_flush {
145:             return None;
146:         }
147:         let bytes = encode_batch(
148:             self.frame_count,
149:             GUEST_TO_HOST,
150:             &self.opcodes,
151:             &self.pending_arena,
152:         );
153:         self.opcodes.clear();
154:         self.pending_arena.clear();
155:         self.last_arena_len = 0;
156:         self.started = None;
157:         self.size_triggered = false;
158:         Some(bytes)
159:     }
160: }

183:         assert!(!bytes.is_empty());
184:         assert!(batcher.is_empty());
185:     }
186:

188:     fn no_flush_when_under_policy() {
189:         let policy = BatchPolicy::new(Duration::from_secs(60), 10_000);
190:         let mut batcher = Batcher::new(policy);
191:         batcher.push_frame(1, &[op(1)], empty_arena());
192:         assert!(!batcher.size_triggered);
193:         assert!(batcher.flush(false).is_none());
194:         // Force flush drains it.

202:         let mut batcher = Batcher::new(policy);

2: 
3: **Last updated:** August 28, 2026
4: 
5: The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a pure function of the
6: opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Protocol contract: `spec/`.
7: 
8: ## Implemented
9: 
10: - **All spec components render**: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `COLOR` (layout-greedy:
11:   `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE`, `VSTACK`/
12:   `HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` (flex), `ZSTACK` (overlay), `GRID`/
13:   `LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` (CSS grid), `SCROLLVIEW`, `BUTTON`, `TEXT_FIELD`
14:   (incl. `IS_SECURE` → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR`, `TOGGLE`
15:   (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`, `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` →
16:   `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children + `SELECTION`), `MENU`,
17:   `COLOR_PICKER`, `COMMENT`.
18: - **Composite override mode**: `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`SLIDER` with children render
19:   the custom body wrapped in the native element.
20: - **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis flex), `CONTENT_MARGINS`,
21:   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL`/`HUG`), `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`,
22:   `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`,
23:   `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `BORDER_*`,
24:   `SELECTED`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`, `ENABLED`, `ROLE`/`STATE` (ARIA).
25: - **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` /
26:   `data-binding-id` attributes.
27: - `STYLE::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time).
28: 
29: ## Not implemented / gaps
30: 
31: - `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property).
32: - GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact.
33:

37: properties, composite, event attrs, `days_to_date`, network-decoded frames).

# pathland-render-html (Rust) — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 28, 2026

The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a pure function of the
opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **All spec components render**: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `COLOR` (layout-greedy:
  `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE`, `VSTACK`/
  `HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` (flex), `ZSTACK` (overlay), `GRID`/
  `LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` (CSS grid), `SCROLLVIEW`, `BUTTON`, `TEXT_FIELD`
  (incl. `IS_SECURE` → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR`, `TOGGLE`
  (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`, `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` →
  `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children + `SELECTION`), `MENU`,
  `COLOR_PICKER`, `COMMENT`.
- **Composite override mode**: `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`SLIDER` with children render
  the custom body wrapped in the native element.
- **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis flex), `CONTENT_MARGINS`,
  `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL`/`HUG`), `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`,
  `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`,
  `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `BORDER_*`,
  `SELECTED`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`, `ENABLED`, `ROLE`/`STATE` (ARIA).
- **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` /
  `data-binding-id` attributes.
- `STYLE::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time).

## Not implemented / gaps

- `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property).
- GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact.

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 22 headless render tests (components,
properties, composite, event attrs, `days_to_date`, network-decoded frames).

257: ## Web Client (SSR HTML + app.js)

259: The browser client is the **SSR HTML renderer** (`pathland-render-html`, and its

261: client — `app.js`, shipped in both demos. It hydrates the server-rendered DOM by
262: `data-pathland-id`, decodes each self-contained `PLPL` batch, applies opcode
263: deltas in place, and sends raw-input events back over the `/ws` socket.
264: 
265: ## Components & Properties
266: 
267: Component and property IDs are defined in `pathland-core`'s
268: [`constants.rs`](./lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs),
269: documented in [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md), and catalogued by category in
270: [PRIMITIVES.md](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md) (component types), [MODIFIERS.md](./spec/MODIFIERS.md)
271: (properties), and [EVENTS.md](./spec/EVENTS.md) (events). Component types
272: include `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `VSTACK`, `HSTACK`, `SPACER`, and more; stack
273: constraint properties (`SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, …) drive native layout, styling
274: modifiers (`PADDING`, `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, …) decorate any view, and
275: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` use `-1` = FILL, `-2` = HUG_CONTENT.
276: 
277: ## Design Tokens
278: 
279: The renderer owns default token values; the application owns overrides.
280: Tokens are identified by dot-separated paths (`color.primary`, `space.2`) and
281: referenced via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type or overridden globally with
282: `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`. See [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system).

### Run tests

```bash
cd lib/rust && cargo test
cd lib/java && mvn test

# no_std / wasm32 direction guard (requires: rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown)
cd lib/rust && ./check-wasm.sh
```

### Run the GTK desktop demo (native, zero-copy shared ring)

```bash
cd lib/rust && PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo
```

## Web Client (SSR HTML + app.js)

The browser client is the **SSR HTML renderer** (`pathland-render-html`, and its
Java counterpart `com.pathland.render.html`), hydrated by a small vanilla-JS
client — `app.js`, shipped in both demos. It hydrates the server-rendered DOM by
`data-pathland-id`, decodes each self-contained `PLPL` batch, applies opcode
deltas in place, and sends raw-input events back over the `/ws` socket.

## Components & Properties

Component and property IDs are defined in `pathland-core`'s
[`constants.rs`](./lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs),
documented in [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md), and catalogued by category in
[PRIMITIVES.md](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md) (component types), [MODIFIERS.md](./spec/MODIFIERS.md)
(properties), and [EVENTS.md](./spec/EVENTS.md) (events). Component types
include `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `VSTACK`, `HSTACK`, `SPACER`, and more; stack
constraint properties (`SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, …) drive native layout, styling
modifiers (`PADDING`, `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, …) decorate any view, and
`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` use `-1` = FILL, `-2` = HUG_CONTENT.

## Design Tokens

The renderer owns default token values; the application owns overrides.
Tokens are identified by dot-separated paths (`color.primary`, `space.2`) and
referenced via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type or overridden globally with
`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`. See [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system).

## POC Goals

See the GitHub issues (#12, #13, #15, #16, #18):

1. **16-byte opcode engine** — done
2. **Core components & modifiers in Rust** (declarative API) — done
3. **Opcode transport layer** (shared memory + network batch + native C-ABI shim) — done
4. **Rust desktop app with GTK4 renderer** (native shared ring) — done
5. **Native Java library set** (hand-written `com.pathland.view` DSL + signals/computed/effects + reusable HTML renderer + state stores) — done
6. **Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo** (SSR HTML via `pathland-render-html` + live 16-byte opcode deltas) — done

## Versioning

Pathland follows **Semantic Versioning** (Major.Minor.Patch). The wire protocol
version is 1 (see [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md)).

## Contributing

Pathland is open to contributors. Please read:

- [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) — how to build, test, and make changes
- [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) — the Contributor Covenant
- [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) — how to report a vulnerability (do **not** open a public issue)

Issues are grouped into milestones `1 · Hardening & Memory Safety` through
`5 · Packaging & Grant Readiness`, labelled by epic (`hardening`,
`benchmarking`, `tooling`, `a11y-seo`, `packaging`).

## License

Pathland is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details.

1: # Security Policy
2: 
3: Pathland is a network-facing binary protocol: the byte decoders and the C ABI
4: are security-critical surfaces. This policy covers how vulnerabilities are
5: reported and handled.
6: 
7: ## Reporting a vulnerability
8: 
9: **Do not open a public issue for a security vulnerability.** Report it privately
10: to the maintainers:
11: 
12: - Email: `michael@apaq.dk`
13: - Subject prefix: `[Pathland security]`
14: 
15: Please include:
16: 
17: - The affected crate/module and version (or commit).
18: - A description of the vulnerability and its impact.
19: - A minimal reproduction (payload bytes or code) where possible.
20: - Any suggested fix, if you have one.
21: 
22: We aim to acknowledge reports within **5 business days** and to ship a fix (or a
23: mitigation) as soon as a coordinated patch is ready. We will credit reporters in
24: the release notes unless anonymity is requested.
25: 
26: ## Scope
27: 
28: The following are in scope for this policy:
29: 
30: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core` — the `no_std` protocol core (opcode decode,
31:   ring buffer, arena, memory layout).
32: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport` — PLPL batch encode/decode.
33: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-capi` — the `unsafe extern "C"` ring ABI
34:   (`libpathland_core`): pointer-argument handling, zero-copy reads, event drain.
35: - `lib/java/pathland-view` `transport` — `FrameCodec` (PLPL encode/decode).
36: - The demos' vanilla-JS `app.js` web client (PLPL batch decode + hydration in
37:   `lib/java/*-demo/src/main/resources`).
38: 
39: Out of scope: dependencies (report those to their respective projects),
40: development-only tooling, and the demo application code.
41:

# Security Policy

Pathland is a network-facing binary protocol: the byte decoders and the C ABI
are security-critical surfaces. This policy covers how vulnerabilities are
reported and handled.

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Do not open a public issue for a security vulnerability.** Report it privately
to the maintainers:

- Email: `michael@apaq.dk`
- Subject prefix: `[Pathland security]`

Please include:

- The affected crate/module and version (or commit).
- A description of the vulnerability and its impact.
- A minimal reproduction (payload bytes or code) where possible.
- Any suggested fix, if you have one.

We aim to acknowledge reports within **5 business days** and to ship a fix (or a
mitigation) as soon as a coordinated patch is ready. We will credit reporters in
the release notes unless anonymity is requested.

## Scope

The following are in scope for this policy:

- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core` — the `no_std` protocol core (opcode decode,
  ring buffer, arena, memory layout).
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport` — PLPL batch encode/decode.
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-capi` — the `unsafe extern "C"` ring ABI
  (`libpathland_core`): pointer-argument handling, zero-copy reads, event drain.
- `lib/java/pathland-view` `transport` — `FrameCodec` (PLPL encode/decode).
- The demos' vanilla-JS `app.js` web client (PLPL batch decode + hydration in
  `lib/java/*-demo/src/main/resources`).

Out of scope: dependencies (report those to their respective projects),
development-only tooling, and the demo application code.

## Security-sensitive guarantees

- Every 16-byte opcode decoder must **reject malformed/truncated input
  gracefully** (no panics, no out-of-bounds reads, no hangs) — see the hardening
  issues (#37, #38).
- The C ABI entry points (`pathland_ring_buffer_push`,
  `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, `pathland_core_drain_events`, …) treat
  caller-provided pointers as trusted by contract; the bounds guarantees must be
  upheld and are audited via Miri/sanitizers in CI.
- No secrets or tokens may ever be committed; see
  [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Security testing

Coverage is tracked by the hardening milestone (issues #37–#39): fuzzing for the
Rust/TypeScript/Java decoders, Miri + ASan/UBSan on the C ABI, and bounds fixes.
Results will be linked here as they land.

## Supported versions

The project is pre-1.0 (`wire protocol version 1`). Security fixes land on the
default branch and are backported only when a tagged release is actively used;
see the [Versioning](README.md#versioning) section.

# pathland-demo-views — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 29, 2026

The framework-agnostic shared demo views (`com.pathland.demo`), consumed by the
Quarkus and Spring Boot demos. Uses `State` fields wired by the
`pathland-view-processor` annotation processor.

## Implemented

- **`KitchenSinkView`** (the demo root): a scrollable column of every protocol
  section, mounted by both demos' `SessionApp`.
- **Sections** (each a custom `View`):
  - `SectionCard` — reusable titled/bordered/rounded section wrapper.
  - `CounterSection` — `State<Integer>` + `Button` + `Stepper`.
  - `TextFieldSection` — `TextField` + `TextEditor` on one `State<String>`.
  - `ToggleSection` — `Toggle` in all three `ToggleStyle`s.
  - `ValueControlsSection` — `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`ProgressView` on one
    `State<Float>`.
  - `PickerSection` — `Picker` (Segmented + Menu) + `Menu`.
  - `ColorSection` — `ColorPicker` + `Color` as a View + reactive `Rectangle`.
  - `DateSection` — `DatePicker` bound to days-since-epoch.
  - `LayoutSection` — `Grid`/`LazyVStack`/`HStack`+`Spacer`/`ZStack`/`Divider`.
  - `TextStylesSection` — text-formatting modifiers.
  - `AppearanceSection` — border/shadow/opacity/transform/hidden/z-index.
- **Legacy views kept**: `CounterView`, `CounterControls`, `NameField` (still
  covered by `CounterViewTest`).

## Not implemented / gaps

- The browser experience depends on the demos' `app.js` hydration client
  (shipped in each demo's `src/main/resources`).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views` (needs JDK 25) — `CounterViewTest`,
`KitchenSinkViewTest` (mount + persistence + input routing).

1: //! Network batch transport (remote path).
2: //!
3: //! Producer side serializes Frames into network batches (opcodes + arena delta);
4: //! the consumer decodes them with `BatchDecoder` (see `crate::batch`) back into
5: //! `Frame` views consumed by `RenderTree::apply_frame`. This is the remote/SSR
6: //! path where producer and consumer do **not** share memory.
7: //!
8: //! The wire format is unchanged from `crate::batch` (magic/version/flags/
9: //! frameCount/opcodeCount/opcodes/arenaDeltaLen/arena).
10: 
11: use alloc::vec::Vec;
12: 
13: use pathland_core::{Frame, Opcode};
14: 
15: use crate::batch::encode_batch;
16: 
17: /// Producer-side network batch encoder.
18: ///
19: /// Buffers opcodes (from Frames) and serializes them into a batch with the
20: /// arena's used-arena slice. Use the `Batcher` helper (`crate::batching`) for a
21: /// time/size flush policy; this type is the bare encoder for explicit flushes.
22: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
23: pub struct NetBatchEncoder {
24:     opcodes: Vec<Opcode>,
25: }
26: 
27: impl NetBatchEncoder {
28:     /// Append a frame's opcodes to the pending batch.
29:     pub fn push_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
30:         self.opcodes.extend(frame.opcodes());
31:     }
32: 
33:     /// Append raw opcodes to the pending batch.
34:     pub fn push_opcodes(&mut self, opcodes: &[Opcode]) {
35:         self.opcodes.extend_from_slice(opcodes);
36:     }
37: 
38:     /// Serialize the pending opcodes with a provided used-arena slice, clearing
39:     /// the buffer. `frame_count` is the covering frame counter.
40:     pub fn encode_with_arena(&mut self, frame_count: u32, arena_used: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
41:         let bytes = encode_batch(
42:             frame_count,
43:             crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST,
44:             &self.opcodes,
45:             arena_used,
46:         );
47:         self.opcodes.clear();
48:         bytes
49:     }
50: 
51:     /// Whether any opcodes are buffered.
52:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
53:         self.opcodes.is_empty()
54:     }
55: 
56:     /// Number of buffered opcodes.
57:     pub fn pending(&self) -> usize {
58:         self.opcodes.len()
59:     }
60: }
61:

71:             Opcode::new(

# pathland-core-transport — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 28, 2026

The **transport** layer: the shared-memory ring owner and the network batch
codec (both directions). Protocol contract: `spec/OPCODE.md` (Transport).

## Implemented

- **`RingTransport`**: zero-copy SPSC shared-memory transport over the
  `pathland-core` linear memory — `next_frame` (guest→host frames as
  `OpcodeBatch`) and `send_input`/`drain_events` (host→guest raw inputs,
  including shared-ring `TEXT_CHANGED` text via the host event arena).
- **Network batch codec** (`batch.rs`, `net.rs`): `encode_batch`/`decode_batch`
  for guest→host frames and `encode_events`/`decode_events` for host→guest
  event batches (`HOST_TO_GUEST` direction flag, `TEXT_CHANGED` text in the
  batch string section, plus all typed draft events — focus/edit/submit/scroll/
  wheel/date-changed). Both directions are fully wired at the codec level.
- **Batching policy** (`batching.rs`): time/size flush thresholds with arena
  delta tracking.
- **Conformance vectors 13/14** (`conformance.rs`): golden network-batch bytes.

- No out-of-the-box duplex *server transport* (WebSocket/session plumbing) in
  this crate — the codecs exist; the Java demos (Quarkus/Spring) wire the
  browser↔server duplex.

`cargo test -p pathland-core-transport` — ring round-trips (incl. zero-copy),
batch encode/decode both directions, batching policy, conformance vectors.

# Pathland — Grant Proposal (Submittable Draft)

**Fund:** NLnet / NGI "Open Internet Stack" — new fund calls reopen **Sept 3, 2026**; deadline **Nov 3, 2026, 12:00 CET**

---

## 1. Applicant

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Legal entity | Apaq ApS |

---

## 2. Problem

Server-driven UI (SDUI) and cross-platform UI are fragmented: each platform
re-invents retained-mode UI inside a closed framework (Flutter, React Native,
Compose Multiplatform, per-vendor SDUI like Airbnb/Lyft/Spotify). The result:

- **No open, language- and platform-agnostic *protocol*** exists for describing
  declarative, retained-mode UI — only frameworks that couple the UI model to a
  specific runtime.

  microcontrollers) to in-browser to server-driven enterprise apps, so teams
  build and maintain N different UI transports.
- **Full-tree serialization is wasteful**: typical SDUI re-sends large JSON
  payloads; large, reactive trees cannot sustain high frame rates on the wire or
  on the main thread.

## 3. Innovation — a standard, not another framework

Pathland describes **WHAT** the UI is — structure + constraint properties
(VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment) — as a stream of **fixed
16-byte opcodes** in a ring buffer, and never **WHERE** (no layout, no rects).
Renderers are **pure functions of the stream**, so the same opcode stream maps
onto native widgets on every platform (GTK4, DOM/HTML, LVGL-planned).

The engine is **transport- and process-agnostic**: the producer and consumer
only need to exchange bytes, so it runs identically across embedded dual-core,
pure in-browser (WASM worker → `SharedArrayBuffer`), native desktop (C ABI /
Java FFM over a zero-copy shared ring), and distributed server-driven modes.

**Emission is diff-based and reactive**: a signal bound to a node re-emits only
that node's deltas; an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. That is what makes
the binary format dramatically smaller than JSON SDUI and fast enough for a
120 FPS interaction target.

The open-standard angle: anyone can implement a Pathland renderer or DSL in any
language against the spec and the golden conformance vectors, with no lock-in to
a runtime.

## 4. The specification (exists — split, not monolithic)

The normative spec is **already present** and is the contract this proposal
matures:

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `spec/OPCODE.md` | 16-byte opcode format, ring buffer, arena, frame lifecycle, value types, design tokens |
| `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` | Primitive views + component IDs |
| `spec/MODIFIERS.md` | Core modifiers/properties + value types + enum codes |
| `spec/EVENTS.md` | Core events + listener bits |
| `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` | Golden byte vectors |
| `spec/DSL.md` | Authoring surface (SwiftUI-shaped DSL contract) — informative |

Gap this proposal fills: a **spec index + consolidated property-key registry**
and a **cross-language validator** so the split files read as one implementable
whole and cannot drift.

## 5. Scope & work packages (core-first)

The **core is the deliverable** (an implementable open standard); the visual
layer is cheap proof, not the product.

| WP | Deliverable | Issue | Effort (h) | Cost @€45/h |
|----|-------------|-------|-----------|-------------|

| WP2 | Machine-readable ID schema + cross-language validator CLI (Rust/Java drift guard) + expanded golden conformance vectors (validation only — codegen deferred) | #43 | 70 | €3,150 |
| WP3 | Coverage-guided fuzz harnesses (Rust/JS/Java), TS `stringAt` bounds fix, one Miri pass on the C ABI | #37, #38 | 70 | €3,150 |
| WP4 | Benchmark suite: 16-byte vs JSON/Protobuf SDUI (payload size, decode latency, memory) + one CI chart | #40 | 30 | €1,350 |
| WP5 | CI completion (rust + java jobs), **WCAG/ARIA compliance on the SSR HTML renderer**, hosted SSR HTML demo (URL + screenshots), evidence pack | #44, #49, #50 | 45 | €2,025 |
| PM / reporting (10%) | NLnet reporting, MoU tracking | — | 15 | €675 |
| **Total** | | | **260 h** | **€11,700** |

## 6. Budget & rates

- **Cost-recovery**, rate **€45/h**, **260 h**, total ask **€11,700**.
- NLnet may adjust ineligible costs; the final amount is settled in the MoU.
- No other funding sources at present.

client). WP5 makes it visible cheaply: host the existing Quarkus SSR demo at a
public URL, include 2 screenshots and the WP4 comparison chart. Reviewers can
click a working multi-renderer demo without the core work being a "black box".

## 8. Prior-art comparison

Airbnb, Lyft and Spotify ship proprietary, per-app SDUI JSON schemas — closed,
not an open standard. Flutter, React Native and Compose Multiplatform are
frameworks that couple the UI model to one runtime. Native toolkits (GTK,
SwiftUI, WinUI) are per-platform and closed. Generic serialization (JSON,
Protobuf) is schema-driven data transport, not a UI instruction stream, and
re-sends full trees. Pathland is a **16-byte command stream** (tree mutations +
properties), open-spec, process/transport-agnostic, with native-element renderers
and zero-copy, diff-based emission — an open standard, not another framework.

## 9. European dimension & ecosystem

- **Digital sovereignty**: an open, Apache-2.0 UI protocol reduces dependence on
  US-owned UI stacks — a "made in Europe" alternative for the Open Internet
  Stack's *independent and cross-platform development framework* area.
- **Open standards / interoperability**: spec + conformance vectors let any EU

- [ ] Schema + validator CLI + expanded conformance vectors, CI-gated (WP2)
- [ ] Fuzz harnesses (Rust/JS/Java) + C ABI Miri pass (WP3)
- [ ] Benchmark suite + comparison chart (WP4)
- [ ] **WCAG/ARIA compliance on the SSR HTML renderer** (WP5)
- [ ] CI green (rust + java), hosted demo URL, screenshots (WP5)
- [ ] NLnet final report + MoU deliverables (PM)

## 12. Two-page narrative (copy-ready for the NLnet form)

**Proposal name:** Pathland — an implementable open UI-protocol standard.

**What it is.** Pathland is an open, Apache-2.0 protocol for declarative,
retained-mode UI that is language- and platform-agnostic. It describes *what* a
UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment — as a stream of fixed
**16-byte opcodes**, never *where*. Emission is diff-based and reactive: only the
nodes that changed emit, an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes, and renderers are
pure functions of the stream that map onto native elements (GTK4, DOM/HTML,
LVGL-planned). The engine is transport- and process-agnostic, running from
embedded dual-core to in-browser WASM to distributed server-driven backends.
The spec already exists (split across `spec/OPCODE`, `PRIMITIVES`, `MODIFIERS`,
`EVENTS`, `CONFORMANCE`, plus the `DSL` authoring surface) and is enforced by
golden byte vectors.

**What we will build.** This project turns the working proof-of-concept into an
**implementable open standard**: (1) a spec index and consolidated
property-key registry; (2) a machine-readable ID schema and cross-language
validator so the four language surfaces cannot drift; (3) coverage-guided fuzzing

(5) CI, **WCAG/ARIA compliance on the HTML renderer**, and a hosted SSR HTML
demo as live evidence. A solo maintainer delivers
this in six months at 260 hours (cost-recovery, €11,700).

**Why it matters.** An open UI *protocol* — rather than another UI *framework* —
lets any EU vendor build renderers and DSLs against one spec, reducing lock-in to
US-owned stacks and supporting the Open Internet Stack's cross-platform
development goal. The 16-byte, zero-delta wire format is an efficiency answer to
bloated JSON SDUI. Prior art (Airbnb/Lyft/Spotify SDUI, Flutter, React Native)
is closed or runtime-coupled; nothing provides an open, diff-based binary
instruction stream across embedded, browser, desktop, and server.

**European dimension.** Made in Denmark; Apache-2.0; engagement with LVGL, W3C

- [ ] Confirm GenAI-disclosure preference (none used in this document's drafting

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'spec/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  rust:
    name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4), so the runner needs
      # the GTK4 system libraries before `cargo test` can link them.
      - name: Install GTK4 system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libgtk-4-dev \
            libglib2.0-dev \
            libcairo2-dev \
            libpango1.0-dev \
            libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
            libgraphene-1.0-dev

      - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: lib/rust -> target

      - name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by Java FFM / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK 25)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # JDK 25 is required (maven.compiler.release=25; ScopedValue JEP 506).
      # Temurin 25 has shipped; if setup-java's manifest lags, swap in a direct
      # Adoptium 25 tarball download for this step.
      - name: Set up JDK 25
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '25'
          cache: maven

      - name: Test reactor (demo modules excluded to keep CI fast)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test -pl '!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'
